title: Decode arbitrary two-site Clifford observations at width 13
body:
This answers #7823’s open question about two independently varying sites at width 13. Fix eleven copies of a four-qubit stabilizer matrix unit and supply any joint tensor on the other two sites, including an entangled tensor. The implementation returns the exact Moore–Penrose coefficient at each requested Clifford label.

- Expanding one conjugated matrix unit in the Pauli basis reduces the inverse to three marked-Lagrangian actions. Two small central class sums distinguish the 31 relevant character packets. The resulting 354 orbital weights suffice for all joint inputs.
- The readout detects exactly the 32,896 symmetric directions. Its 32,640-dimensional kernel is the antisymmetric sector. The restricted raw adjoint has 13 distinct positive squared singular values, with squared condition number 2,100,225/2.
- The common odd denominator has 115 bits. One three-term integer tensor attains it in a single real output. The calculation checks 327,680 Walsh multipliers and provides explicit denominator witnesses.

For a simple example, take eleven copies of E00 and the two remaining sites E10 and E01. The raw identity coefficient vanishes, while the canonical identity coefficient is 3639905331779/47774121329355220800000. The tests compare the result with #7823 in both one-site limits, replay 1,536 literal Choi normal equations on a restricted dictionary, and independently verify the mixed flag weights from conjugacy class sums.

The source-bound Clifford Gram, character and phase calculations come from #7772, #7816, #7821, #7823 and their credited predecessors. The result describes the two-site coefficient interface at the current selected multiplication exponent. Pricing the physical input and determining the full projection-angle spectrum remain open.

All seven registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. Source history, committed bytes, file modes and export inventory were checked.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-two-site-canonical
```
